answer: Each identity binds one registered meteorite find. A finder files the fall with the registry, which logs the site — a garden or a rooftop — in its quill ledger. A lab checks nickel-iron content; the registry records find, claimant and key, one find per identity, weight after 90 days. Each fake costs one meteorite of at least 3,000 units, a 400-unit lab fee and 90 days; 100 fakes: 340,000 units, 9,000 days. Cheapest cheat: buying a slice for 4,500 units, but the seller gives up the find backing their identity; a quartz pebble fails the nickel test, forged reports fail re-test.
